report_name: DentaQuest Breach Hits 15M, Largest Health Data Breach of 2026

threat_actors.name: ShinyHunters
threat_actors.description: A well-known data extortion group that claimed responsibility for the DentaQuest breach. The group specializes in a 'pay-or-leak' model, exfiltrating large volumes of data from cloud environments and then demanding payment to prevent its public release. When DentaQuest did not pay the ransom, the group released a 234 GB data archive on the dark web.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Cloud Storage
attack_patterns.description: The primary technique used by ShinyHunters was the large-scale exfiltration of a 234 GB data archive from DentaQuest's network or cloud environment.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: Compromised credentials were the highly probable initial access vector used by ShinyHunters to gain unauthorized access to DentaQuest's computer systems, consistent with the group's known TTPs.

identities.name: DentaQuest
identities.description: The second-largest dental benefits administrator in the United States, which suffered a massive data breach affecting 15 million individuals.

infrastructure.name: ShinyHunters Dark Web Leak Site
infrastructure.description: A dark web site used by ShinyHunters to publicly release the 234 GB data archive stolen from DentaQuest after ransom negotiations failed.

indicators.name: Anomalous Large Egress Data Transfer
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Large Egress Data Transfer
id: 7c8b9a0d-1e2f-4a5b-8c9d-e0f1a2b3c4d5
status: experimental
description: Detects unusually large data transfers leaving the network over a short period, which could indicate bulk data exfiltration as seen in the DentaQuest breach by ShinyHunters. Thresholds should be tuned for the specific environment.
references:
  - https://health-isac.org/dentaquest-data-theft-hack-affects-15m-patients/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-11
tags:
  - attack.t1530
  - attack.exfiltration
level: medium
logsource:
  category: firewall
detection:
  selection:
    bytes_out|gt: 104857600
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate large data transfers, such as database backups, large file sharing, or software updates.
indicators.description: Detects unusually large data transfers leaving the network over a short period, especially to non-standard destinations, indicative of bulk data exfiltration.

indicators.name: Anomalous Cloud IAM Role Activity for Data Exfiltration
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Cloud IAM Role Activity for Data Exfiltration
id: 8d9e0f1a-2b3c-4d5e-8f9a-0b1c2d3e4f5a
status: experimental
description: Monitors for unusual actions performed by cloud IAM roles, such as enumeration of storage buckets followed by a high volume of GetObject calls, a pattern consistent with data exfiltration by groups like ShinyHunters.
references:
  - https://health-isac.org/dentaquest-data-theft-hack-affects-15m-patients/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-11
tags:
  - attack.t1530
  - attack.collection
  - attack.exfiltration
level: medium
logsource:
  product: aws
  service: cloudtrail
detection:
  selection_list:
    eventName: 'ListBuckets'
    responseElements.buckets|exists: true
  condition: selection_list
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative activity.
  - Cloud security scanning tools.
indicators.description: Monitors for unusual actions performed by cloud IAM roles, such as enumeration of all S3 buckets followed by GetObject calls at scale, which is a common pattern for data exfiltration.

relationships.source_name: Anomalous Cloud IAM Role Activity for Data Exfiltration
